$comment: Two layers, read by `pnpm prod:list-values`. `minimum`: the presentation floor — the list builder shows 20 values before search, so a list below it is shallow. Floors (`default`, `groups`, `lists`): the catalog depth target that `gap` measures. Floor precedence: --floor N, then lists[category slug], then types[entity type slug], then groups[group slug], then default. A list's normal target is its type's, else its group's, else the default; a `lists` entry below that marks it bounded. Compatibility, lifestyle, money, home, career and travel lists use the default 30, except narrow personality/routine/habit types at 28 (`types`); entertainment and taste domains 40; broad canonical lists 50. A list whose domain honestly can't reach its floor gets its own lower entry here rather than padded values.
